title: Jurisdictional Snapshotter: automated retention snapshots & chain-of-custody for SOC 2/ISO audits
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Private / Dedicated need a defensible, time-bounded artifact that proves where data lived and what retention policy was applied for a given period. Current evidence pipelines produce per-control artifacts but lack a compact, tamper-evident snapshot that ties retention config, active data residency policy, and the collector run state together for auditor consumption.

Goal: Build a "Jurisdictional Snapshotter" that produces a single signed bundle per jurisdiction/time-window containing: (1) retention policy config and applied version, (2) active residency routing table and tags, (3) collector run metadata (IDs, start/end, checksums), (4) a digest of sampled artifacts and locations (S3 paths, DB snapshot refs), and (5) chain-of-custody events (who/what changed policies) to support SOC 2 and ISO 27001 evidence requests. The bundle should be exportable, cryptographically hashed, and linkable to the existing evidence index.

Scope: Prototype for Hosted + Dedicated modes, design export format (JSONL + metadata manifest + signature), integration points with Evidence Collector, Residency Router, and Audit Index. Exclude full data export or retrieval of raw PII content; only include references and hashes.

Non-goals: bulk data migration tooling, long-term cold storage lifecycle policy engine (that remains a separate job), or replacing existing per-control artifacts (this complements them).
acceptance_criteria: Produces a per-jurisdiction snapshot bundle on demand and scheduled cadence (daily, weekly) as configured in project settings

Bundle includes: retention_config.json (versioned), residency_table.json (routing tags), collector_run_manifest.json (ids, timestamps, checksums), artifact_index.csv (paths + sha256), and snapshot.manifest (bundle metadata + signature)
Snapshot bundles are written to configured evidence storage (S3 or GCS) under a predictable prefix and registered in Audit Index with a stable snapshot ID
Bundles are signed using the customer's KMS key in Private mode or Redwood signing key in Hosted mode; signature verification endpoint available for auditors
Ability to retrieve snapshot metadata (not raw payload) from Console and to attach snapshot IDs to control evidence rows in the Console UI
Performance: generating a daily snapshot for a mid-sized tenant (<50M tokens / 10TB logs refs) completes within 30 minutes; does not significantly increase collector CPU usage during window
Security review completed and threat model updated to show no new PII exposure vectors (metadata-only by default)
E2E smoke test and example auditor report generated and stored in artifacts/ with a sample customer fixture
tasks: Design: format spec for snapshot bundle (manifest schema, minimal fields, sampling policy) - owner: Design
Infra: storage prefixes, lifecycle tags, and IAM permissions for snapshot writer - owner: Infra
Runtime: hook Evidence Collector to produce collector_run_manifest and artifact index - owner: Eng Collector
Routing: export residency routing table and tag versions from Residency Router - owner: Eng Routing
KMS: integrate signing flow for Private (customer KMS) and Hosted (Redwood signing) - owner: Security
Console: add snapshot registry view and attach snapshot IDs to control evidence rows - owner: Console PM/Eng
Docs: Confluence runbook for auditors describing retrieval and verification process - owner: PM
QA: load test on a synthetic mid-sized tenant and run security checklist - owner: QA

2025-01-23 - Liam Cortez: Engineering spike completed. PoC created that assembles a manifest and writes bundle to s3://redwood-evidence-proto/PM-135001/. PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evidence/pull/482 (draft)
